title: Dedicated: Fleet autoscaler - burst controls + utilization reporting (v28)
author: Diego Morales
release_notes: Improved fleet autoscaler to respect per-fleet burst budgets; added utilization reporting metrics and Grafana dashboards. No user-facing breaking changes.
description:
Context: Customers on Dedicated requested stronger controls for short-term burst capacity (to handle spiky traffic) while preserving long-term throughput guarantees and clearer utilization telemetry for billing/ops. This PR implements a token-bucket burst mechanism in the Dedicated fleet autoscaler, ties burst accounting into existing throughput guarantees, and expands utilization reporting for per-fleet and per-customer views.

What this PR does: 1) Autoscaler: introduces a burst token bucket that lets fleets temporarily scale above target capacity when credits are available. The bucket is configured at the fleet level with: bucket_size, refill_rate, and a circuit breaker threshold to prevent runaway scale-ups. 2) Throughput guarantees: scale decisions now consider both steady-state target throughput and burst credit balance so that temporary spikes do not violate long-term reserved throughput. 3) Telemetry: emits new metrics (fleet.burst_credits, fleet.burst_spent, fleet.peak_scale_factor, fleet.utilization_5m/1h) and tags (fleet_id, customer_org). These are aggregated in our metrics pipeline and wired to a new Grafana dashboard for Dedicated customers. 4) Migration: includes a small data migration to initialize burst buckets for existing fleets with a conservative default. 5) Tests & safety: unit tests for token bucket accounting, integration smoke to validate scale flow, and e2e scenario that replays a production spike trace. 6) Ops/UI: Console changes to display burst quota and historical usage on the fleet detail page.

Why: Previously the autoscaler could either be too conservative (dropping client requests under bursty workloads) or too aggressive (permanently scaling and increasing cost). This design provides predictable short-term headroom while preserving long-run throughput SLAs. The expanded telemetry helps SRE and billing to explain utilization and cost anomalies.

Migration notes: The migration (migrations/20250115_init_burst_buckets.sql) sets default bucket_size=10*instance_cap and refill_rate=1 token/min per instance for existing fleets. Customers can tune via fleet API or Console.

Related: ENG-1789 (autoscaler refactor), SUP-4123 (customer reported burst overage), several prior PRs in this series (see PR chain included in commits).

Emit new telemetry metrics and tagging (observability/metrics/broadcast.go)

review_conversation: Ava Chen: Can we make the bucket defaults configurable via Helm and expose them in the Console? (comment)
Author Diego Morales: Yes — added helm values and Console panel. Defaults come from migrations but can be overridden per-fleet. (reply)
Marcus Li: I worry about thundering-herd scale-ups in region with constrained capacity. Can we add a regional circuit breaker? (request changes)
Diego Morales: Added region-level circuit breaker that limits aggregate burst scale factor to configured percentage. Unit tests updated. (reply)
Priya Nair: LGTM after test coverage confirmed and small nits fixed in docs. (approved)
merge_outcome: Merged via squash-merge. Commit message summarizes burst autoscaler, migration, and telemetry. Post-merge actions: run migration on prod frozen window (SRE scheduled 2025-02-02), notify account managers of default burst quotas.
notes_for_ops: SRE: migration creates burst columns and initializes values; rollback plan is to drop columns and revert helm config. Monitor new metrics fleet.burst_credits and fleet.peak_scale_factor during ramp. Alert rule added: if fleet.peak_scale_factor > 5x for >10m, page SRE.
qa_notes: Manual test plan included in e2e/tests/dedicated_burst_scenario.py. Steps: 1) create test fleet with instance_cap=4; 2) replay spike trace; 3) verify burst credits consumed and fleet scales up temporarily; 4) verify metrics emitted and Console shows burst history; 5) verify no long-term scale remains after refill.
